findings.evidence: Line 101 `/-- The purely transverse component `F^{ij}`... -/ | transverse` versus lines 408-410, where the bilinear disjunct is `{fieldStrength .plusTransverse, fieldStrength .plusTransverse}` and the single-field disjunct is `{fieldStrength .transverse}`.
findings.fix: In all four places call `F^{+i}` by name or "the good component `F^{+i}`", and reserve "transverse" for `F^{ij}`, e.g. line 64: "...a bilinear in good quark fields or in two `F^{+i}`, or a single `F^{+-}` or `F^{ij}`".
findings.issue: "transverse field strengths" is used to mean `F^{+i}` (`fieldStrength .plusTransverse`), but the file names `F^{ij}` `FieldStrengthComponent.transverse` (line 101: "The purely transverse component `F^{ij}`"). Read with the file's own vocabulary, line 64 says a twist-two neutral operator can be a bilinear in `F^{ij}`, which is twist four and not in the statement. Same wording at lines 68-69, 406 ("`F^{+i} F^{+j}` in transverse field strengths") and 420-421 ("a transverse field strength", "three transverse field strengths").

findings.evidence: Line 89 `| good` under `inductive QuarkProjection`; line 27 "good quark fields and `F^{+i}` have twist one"; statement at line 339 is `∀ f ∈ O, f.twist = 1`.
findings.fix: Either state "every field has twist one" in both docstrings, or add one clause to the intro declaring `F^{+i}` the good gluon component so the term is defined before use.
findings.issue: "all its fields are good components" (and line 56, "every field is a good component") uses "good" for every twist-one field, including `F^{+i}`, but the only formal `good` in the file is `QuarkProjection.good` = `ψ_+`; the intro (line 27) names "good quark fields and `F^{+i}`" separately and never extends "good" to the gluon component.

summary: The module and declaration docstrings are otherwise accurate and match their statements, but "transverse field strength" is used for `F^{+i}` while the file's own constructor `FieldStrengthComponent.transverse` denotes `F^{ij}`, which makes the summary of the quark-number-neutral classifications read as a wrong statement; "good component" is likewise used for all twist-one fields while `good` is a constructor of `QuarkProjection` only.
